about: The fish juveniles, per species (Pierre, 2026-11-19, Q435: four classes become a per-species label for the analyses, with no effect on the game; 15:35: source every juvenile that external sources describe). For each species with juvenile photos in the game: cls, its class (off, finer, bold, like: the juvenile difficulty study's section 4, the definitions in classes), by (source: its own sources rate it; entry: its IMR entry's juvenile class in tools/fish_source.json juv, entry naming it), line (one plain sentence on the juvenile, shown on its species sheet), differs (how it differs from the adult), look (a look-alike a source names, a game species present in the Philippines), ease (a source's words on how easy or hard it is), src [{t, u, q: the quote}], each page read on 2026-11-19. none: the species searched with no source found. Built into fish.json species jv {c, line, src [{t, u}], look} by tools/build_fish.py (juveniles), which checks it; the draw, the ease and the judging never read it (tests/fishjuv.test.js).

classes.off: A source says the juvenile resembles another family, an object or another animal (not where the IMR entry's class A or early list, Pierre's, names it).
classes.finer: A source says it is nearly identical to, very similar to or confused with the juvenile of another species of its genus or family, or that it lacks the mark of its genus or species; or its entry's late list for Halichoeres and Thalassoma ("alike across species").
classes.bold: A source calls it distinctive, easily recognised or unmistakable; or its entry's class A or early list.
classes.like: A source says it is like the adult (or the females or males), or names only differences of degree in the adult's pattern; or its entry's class C.

Platax pinnatus.line: Dark brown to black with a brilliant orange to crimson margin around the body and its very long fins; resembles a toxic flatworm.
Platax pinnatus.differs: Adults have short dorsal and anal fins.

src.q: The stunning juveniles are dark brownish to black with a brilliant orange to crimson margin surrounding the body and their elongate fins.
They mimic a toxic flatworm in shape, colour and movement.
Unlike juveniles, the adults have short dorsal and anal fins.
Juveniles black with bright orange margin around body and fins, fins extremely high and curved in small individuals.

Platax teira.line: Very small juveniles brownish, resembling floating leaves; larger ones with very long pelvic, dorsal and anal fins.
Platax teira.differs: Fins far taller relative to the body than the adult's.

src.q: Very small juveniles are brownish and resemble floating leaves.
Larger juveniles have the pelvic fins and anterior soft rays of the dorsal and anal fins very elongated - reaching to about the rear of the anal-fin base.

Plectorhinchus chaetodonoides.line: Brownish sweetlips with large, well-defined creamy-white blotches; small juveniles swim with exaggerated fin movements and may resemble a toxic flatworm.
Plectorhinchus chaetodonoides.differs: It becomes greyish with large deep-brown spots; the tail turns from deeply forked with rounded lobes to slightly forked.
Plectorhinchus chaetodonoides.ease: Small juveniles may mimic a toxic flatworm

src.q: juveniles brownish with large, well-defined creamy white blotches on body that include brown spots with age; gradually becoming greyish with large, deep brown spots.
Small juveniles may mimic a toxic flatworm
Caudal fin deeply forked with broadly rounded lobes in juveniles; only slightly forked to emarginate in adults.

Plectorhinchus lineatus.line: Sweetlips with a few dark brown bands along the body, which become more diagonal and subdivide with growth.
Plectorhinchus lineatus.differs: The adult is dark brown above with a network of fine white lines, and bright yellow lips and fins.

src.q: Juveniles and subadult fish have black horizontal stripes along the body that become increasingly diagonal with growth.

Colour of juveniles with few horizontal to slightly oblique dark brown bands which subdivide with age until the body appears to be dark chocolate brown above, with a network of fine white lines running up and back

Plectorhinchus polytaenia.line: Like the adult stripes, but with striped fins and fewer stripes on the body.
Plectorhinchus polytaenia.differs: Juveniles have fewer body stripes and striped fins; the fin stripes disappear with age.

src.q: juveniles have fins striped and fewer stripes on body

Plectorhinchus vittatus.line: Sweetlips with a yellow head, irregular broad black stripes or connected blotches, and black pectoral fins.
Plectorhinchus vittatus.differs: The blotches break up into stripes; adults have 6-12 dark stripes and yellow pectoral fins.

src.q: Juveniles have a yellow head, irregular broad black stripes on head and body.
juveniles with connected black blotches and spots that gradually break up into horizontal stripes; pectoral fins black in juveniles becoming uniform yellow in adults

Plectroglyphidodon lacrymatus.line: Dark damsel with bright blue spots, more numerous than the adult's.
Plectroglyphidodon lacrymatus.differs: The blue spots fade and become fewer with age.

src.q: Juveniles have brighter and more numerous blue spots than adults

Plectropomus laevis.line: Resembles the Black-saddled toby, a pufferfish.

src.q: Juveniles mimic the poisonous Blacksaddle Toby, Canthigaster valentini .
Juveniles may mimic the pufferfish Canthigaster valentini .

Plotosus lineatus.line: Brightly striped catfish, often in dense schools of hundreds.
Plotosus lineatus.differs: Adults are solitary or in small groups and shelter under ledges by day.

src.q: Brightly-striped juveniles often form dense schools of hundreds of individuals that appear to move as one.

Pogonoperca punctata.line: Dark brown with many large white spots.
Pogonoperca punctata.differs: Adults are brown with small white spots, a black bar through the eye and four black saddles.

src.q: Juveniles are dark brown with many large white spots.

Pomacanthus imperator.line: Dark blue with electric-blue and white rings, and a white margin on the dorsal fin.

src.q: Juveniles are dark blue with electric blue and white rings, and a white margin on the dorsal fin.
Juveniles are distinguished by a white dorsal-fin margin
Juveniles with blue concentric curved lines on dark body, the innermost of which forming a circle just in front of tail base.

Pomacanthus navarchus.line: Narrow vertical blue and white bands.

src.q: Juveniles with narrow vertical blue and white bands.

Pomacanthus semicirculatus.line: Dark blue with narrow electric-blue and white curved bars, blue fin margins, no concentric rings.
Pomacanthus semicirculatus.differs: Curved lines but no complete circle, unlike the P. imperator juvenile.

src.q: Juveniles are dark blue with narrow electric blue and white curved bars, blue fin margins, and no concentric rings.
Juveniles with curved blue and white lines on dark body, lacking complete circular marking of P. imperator (Emperor Angelfish).

Pomacanthus sexstriatus.line: White vertical bars on a dark body, grading to blue above and below.

src.q: Juvenile with white vertical bars in dark central body, bars grading to blue above and below.

Pomacentrus amboinensis.line: Juveniles have an eyespot on the rear of the dorsal fin.

src.q: Juveniles have an ocellus or false 'eye spot' on the rear of the dorsal fin.

Pomacentrus brachialis.line: Bluish-grey with bright blue fin margins, with the adult's pectoral-fin spot.
Pomacentrus brachialis.differs: Bright blue fin margins; the pectoral-fin spot is shared with the adult.

src.q: Juveniles also have the pectoral-fin spot and are bluish-grey with bright blue fin margins.

Pomacentrus philippinus.line: Like the adult, with a larger yellow-to-orange area at the rear of the body and fins.
Pomacentrus philippinus.differs: The yellow-orange rear area is more expanded than in adults.

src.q: Juveniles have an expanded yellow-to-orange area posteriorly on the body, encompassing the soft dorsal and anal fins, the caudal fin, and the adjacent caudal peduncle.

Pomacentrus tripunctatus.line: Paler damselfish with an eyespot on the upper tail base, a large eyespot on the rear of the dorsal fin, and iridescent blue lines on the head and back.
Pomacentrus tripunctatus.differs: Juveniles are paler and carry the eyespots and blue lines.

src.q: Juveniles are paler with an ocellus on the upper caudal peduncle and an additional large ocellus on the rear of the dorsal fin, and iridescent blue lines on the head and back.

Pomacentrus vaiuli.line: Bright yellow above, deep blue below.

src.q: Juveniles are a bright yellow above becoming deep blue below.

Pseudanthias huchtii.line: Coloured like the females, with green eyes.
Pseudanthias huchtii.differs: Same colours as females; only the green eyes differ.

src.q: Juveniles same colouration as females but with green eyes.

Pseudobalistes flavimarginatus.line: More yellowish, with black spots on the rear of the head and body and saddle-like marks on the back.

src.q: Juveniles are more yellowish with black spots on the rear of the head and body, and saddle-like markings on the back.
Juveniles tend towards yellow.

Pseudodax moluccanus.line: Pale blue wrasse with a broad stripe along the middle of the body, resembling the cleaner wrasses (Labroides); it also cleans other fishes.
Pseudodax moluccanus.differs: Subadults gain a yellow band on the tail base.
Pseudodax moluccanus.ease: Juveniles resemble cleaner wrasse of the genus Labroides

src.q: Juveniles are pale blue with a broad midbody stripe, and subadults have a yellow band on the tail base.
Juveniles resemble cleaner wrasse of the genus Labroides and also remove external parasites form other fishes.

Ptereleotris evides.line: Paler than the adult, with a large oval black spot on the lower tail base.

src.q: Juveniles paler, with large oval black spot on lower caudal-fin base.
Juveniles with extremely long and flexible pectoral fin rays.

Pygoplites diacanthus.line: Like the adult with fewer bands on the side, a large eyespot on the rear of the dorsal fin, and no dark patch around the eye.
Pygoplites diacanthus.differs: Fewer bands, a dorsal-fin eyespot, no dark eye patch.

src.q: Juveniles have fewer bands on the sides, a large ocellus on the rear of the dorsal fin, and lack the dark patch around the eye.

Rhinomuraena quaesita.line: Jet-black ribbon eel with a yellow dorsal fin.
Rhinomuraena quaesita.differs: Males become bright blue with a yellow snout, lower jaw and dorsal fin; females become yellow.

src.q: Juveniles and subadults are jet black with a yellow dorsal fin.
Small juveniles are jet black and develop a yellow dorsal fin.
Males are bright blue with a yellow snout, lower jaw and dorsal fin.
Juveniles all black, males have yellow dorsal fin and females change to a nearly all yellow color, but usually with blue in the posterior

Scarus altipinnis.line: Striped to mottled body with a yellow head.
Scarus altipinnis.ease: small juveniles have a striped to mottled body with a distinctive yellow head

src.q: small juveniles have a striped to mottled body with a distinctive yellow head.
Female S. prasiognathos have more spots on body and markings on face, but very similar juveniles.

Scarus forsteni.line: Very small juveniles off-white to pale brown with four brown stripes; larger ones pale brown with a pale dot near the pectoral-fin tip.

src.q: Very small juveniles (less than 25mm) are off white to pale brown, with 4 brown stripes and pale dots in the orbital and pectoral stripes.

Scarus frenatus.line: White tail, black speckles on the dorsal and anal fins, light stripes from the face fading along the body.

src.q: juveniles have white tail, black speckles on dorsal and anal fins, and light stripes from face disppearing along the body.

Scarus niger.line: Dark greenish black covered in small white spots, with a white band on the tail base edged by two black spots.

src.q: Juveniles are dark greenish black, covered in small white spots, with a black spot at the top and bottom of a white band on the tail base.
Juveniles with pair of black spots on white tail base.

Scarus oviceps.line: Juvenile and female with a single light bar on the upper side.

src.q: S. oviceps juvenile and female have single light bar on upper side.

Scarus rubroviolaceus.line: Young often red or grey with dark scale edges.

src.q: Young stages often red or grey, with dark scale edges.

Scolopsis affinis.line: Monocle bream with a dusky brown stripe on each side of the back's midline and another along the middle of the side, yellowish above at the front.

src.q: Juveniles with dusky brown stripe on either side of dorsal midline, and dusky brown midlateral stripe, yellowish above anteriorly.

Scolopsis bilineata.line: Alternating black and yellow stripes on the upper half, whitish below; resembles the fangblenny Meiacanthus grammistes.
Scolopsis bilineata.differs: The adult is dark grey above with a diagonal black-edged white band and a white blotch under the rear dorsal fin.
Scolopsis bilineata.ease: Batesian mimic of the poison-fanged blenny Meiacanthus grammistes

src.q: juveniles with alternating black and yellow stripes on the upper half and whitish below, Batesian mimic of the poison-fanged blenny Meiacanthus grammistes
Colour dark grey on head and back with diagonal black-edged white band separating dark area from the rest of the mainly whitish body; white blotch below posterior dorsal fin
Juveniles mimic the Linespot Fangblenny, Meiacanthus grammistes which has venomous fangs.

Scolopsis lineata.line: White monocle bream with three black chequerboard-like bars or blotches on the upper side and a black spot between the first three dorsal spines.

src.q: Juveniles are white with three black chequerboard-like bars or blotches on the upper side, and a black spot between first three dorsal spines.
Juveniles white, with 3 black bands on upper half of body, interspace between lower pair of yellow bands; black spot between first three dorsal spines.

Seriola dumerili.line: Clear fins and a series of bands along the body that often appear divided.
Seriola dumerili.differs: Adults brownish to bluish-grey above, silvery-white below, with a dark band through the eye; no body bands.

src.q: Small juveniles have clear fins and a series of bands along the body that often appear divided.

A large predatory jack with a brownish to bluish-grey body becoming silvery-white below, a dusky to dark stripe from the snout to just before the dorsal fin, and a dusky band from the upper jaw through the eye to the first dorsal fin.

Siganus corallinus.line: Small juveniles have narrow blue vertical lines on the sides, which break up into eyespots (ocelli) as they grow.
Siganus corallinus.differs: Blue lines in very small juveniles (up to 50 mm SL), fragmenting into ocelli with growth.

src.q: Small juveniles have narrow blue vertical lines on the sides that fragment into ocelli with growth.
Very small juveniles (up to 50 mm SL) may have vertical blue lines on side, fragmenting into the ocelli with increase in size.

Solenostomus paradoxus.line: Newly settled young almost fully transparent and more slender than the benthic adults.
Solenostomus paradoxus.differs: Transparent and slimmer; colour comes after settling.

src.q: Post-pelagic are almost fully transparent and more slender compared to those established in the benthic phase

Sphyraena barracuda.line: Large dark blotches scattered irregularly along the sides; forked tail.
Sphyraena barracuda.differs: Adults have oblique dark bars on the upper half and a tail with large lobes.

src.q: juveniles with a series of large dark blotches irregularly arranged on sides of body
except young less than 50 cm TL which have a forked caudal fin.

Stethojulis bandanensis.line: Keeps the reddish spot above the pectoral-fin base; small eyespots on the rear dorsal fin and tail base.
Stethojulis bandanensis.differs: Keeps the reddish spot above the pectoral-fin base; adds small eyespots on the rear dorsal fin and tail base.

src.q: A wrasse with a distinctive reddish spot above the pectoral-fin base at all life stages.
Juvenile have small ocelli on the rear of the dorsal fin and tail base.
Juveniles with small ocelli on rear of dorsal fin and tail base.

Stethojulis interrupta.line: Like the females: pinkish-grey above, white below, a broad black stripe; often a yellow snout and black mottling behind the pectoral fin.
Stethojulis interrupta.ease: Females and juveniles highly variable ... this can be difficult to see in dark/striped forms.

src.q: Juveniles are pinkish-grey above, white below, with a broad black stripe running along the sides, and a thin blue line below the eye in larger juveniles.
Females and juveniles highly variable, but often have yellow snout and distinct black mottling pattern (like a mackerel) behind pectoral fin - but this can be difficult to see in dark/striped forms.

Stethojulis strigiventer.line: Small eyespots on the rear dorsal fin and tail base, like S. bandanensis, but with stripes on the underside.
Stethojulis strigiventer.ease: Juveniles with small ocelli on rear dorsal fin and tail base, like S. bandanensis , but the latter lacks stripes on underside.

src.q: Juveniles with small ocelli on rear dorsal fin and tail base, like S. bandanensis , but the latter lacks stripes on underside.

Sufflamen bursa.line: Like the adult; the scythe mark across the pectoral base is yellowish-tan to green.
Sufflamen bursa.differs: The scythe mark's colour differs in juveniles and subadults.

src.q: The characteristic scythe mark crossing the pectoral base is yellowish-tan to green in juveniles and subadults.

Sufflamen chrysopterum.line: Triggerfish dark brown above and white below, with a dark horseshoe-shaped mark on the tail.
Sufflamen chrysopterum.differs: The adult's colour is variable, its pectoral-base bar yellow or black.

src.q: Small juveniles are dark brown above and white below with a dark horseshoe-shaped mark on the tail.
Adult variable in color; the bar running through the pectoral base can either be yellow or black

Synchiropus splendidus.line: Settled juveniles already have the adult's large head and triangular body.
Synchiropus splendidus.differs: Shape as the adult from settlement; colours come later.

src.q: After 12 to 14 days, which is the settlement stage, juveniles look like the adults with a large head,and a triangular shaped body.

Taeniura lymma.line: Born as a miniature version of the adult, about 13-14 cm across.

src.q: Females bear litters of up to seven young, each a miniature version of the adult measuring around 13–14 cm (5.1–5.5 in) across.

Thalassoma amblycephalum.line: Identified by its colour pattern and rounded snout.
Thalassoma amblycephalum.differs: Males become brightly coloured, the head usually green with a yellow band behind it.
Thalassoma amblycephalum.ease: Juveniles easily identified by the color pattern and rounded snout.

src.q: Juveniles easily identified by the color pattern and rounded snout.
Males become brightly colored and head usually green with a yellow band following on the body

Thalassoma jansenii.line: Large juveniles are mostly black with one white band, and white below the head to the anus.
Thalassoma jansenii.differs: Same pattern as females; males keep the white band, more yellow, and add a second narrow band.

src.q: Large juveniles and females are mostly black with a single white band and white area below the head to the anus.

Thalassoma lunare.line: Juveniles have a large dark spot in the middle of the dorsal fin and a large diffuse black spot at the tail base.

src.q: Juveniles with a large dark spot in middle of dorsal fin and a large diffuse black spot at base of caudal fin

Trachyrhamphus bicoarctatus.line: A pipefish with a straight snout and a tiny rounded tail fin.
Trachyrhamphus bicoarctatus.differs: The snout curves and the tail fin is often lost in subadults and adults.

src.q: snout straight in small fish (<150 mm SL), curved in subadults-adults
caudal fin tiny, elongate and rounded in juveniles, but often lost, regenerated, vestigial or represented by stubby rudimentary rays in subadults-adults

Tylosurus crocodilus.line: Needlefish with a raised black lobe at the rear of the dorsal fin.
Tylosurus crocodilus.differs: The black lobe is lost with growth.

src.q: juveniles (to 20 cm body length) with elevated black lobe in posterior part of dorsal fin which is lost with growth

Variola albimarginata.line: Coloured like the adult but with fewer, larger pale blue or pink spots; swims well above the bottom like a basslet.
Variola albimarginata.differs: Similar in colour to adults, with fewer and larger pale blue or pink spots.

src.q: juveniles similar in colour to adults, but with relatively fewer and larger pale blue or pink spots
Juveniles inshore on algae and soft coral reefs, usually swimming well above the substrate, looking much like a basslet

Zebrasoma scopas.line: Yellowish bars and more prominent yellow specks than the adult.
Zebrasoma scopas.differs: Adults are darker with fainter specks.

src.q: Small juveniles have yellowish bars and more prominent yellow specks than adults.

Zebrasoma velifer.differs: Adults are brownish with broad grey-brown bars between narrow yellow ones.

src.q: Small juveniles have alternating yellow and black bars.
